title: Shah Rukh Khan's Knight Riders Just Became the First Cricket Franchise in the World to Own a Stadium
excerpt: The Knight Riders Cricket Ground at Fairplex in Pomona opens with an MLC match, a Bollywood-sized dream, and a straight line to the 2028 Olympics.
body:
The Knight Riders Group — the franchise empire co-owned by Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan, actress Juhi Chawla, and Jay Mehta — has become the first cricket franchise on the planet to own a dedicated cricket stadium. The Knight Riders Cricket Ground at Fairplex in Pomona, California, officially opened its doors on July 1, hosting a Major League Cricket (MLC) match between the Los Angeles Knight Riders and Washington Freedom.

It did not go as planned on the field. Washington Freedom bowled out the hosts for just 108, with Colin Munro's 24 the top score for a Knight Riders batting lineup that never found its footing. Steven Smith's unbeaten 40 steered Washington Freedom to a comfortable six-wicket victory. Andre Russell managed to dismiss Mark Chapman, but it was not enough to rescue the night.

The result, though, will be a footnote in a story that is really about infrastructure. No cricket franchise — not in the IPL, not in the Big Bash, not in the Caribbean Premier League — has ever owned a stadium. The Knight Riders have done it in Southern California, a region home to one of the largest Indian diaspora populations in the United States.

## 'A Place Built Not Just for Sports'

Shah Rukh Khan marked the milestone with a post on X (formerly Twitter) that carried the kind of emotional weight he usually reserves for film premieres.

"What started as a dream… turns into reality today," he wrote. "Welcoming you all to the Knight Riders Cricket Ground, LA. A place built not just for sports but also entertainment and for families… and memories that last forever."

He thanked ICC Chairman Jay Shah and Sanjog Gupta, the media executive who has been central to cricket's American push, calling their support instrumental. Khan closed with the franchise's signature rallying cry: "Believe in Purple and Gold."

The Knight Riders Group already operates franchises in four countries — Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL, Trinbago Knight Riders in the CPL, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the ILT20, and now the Los Angeles franchise in MLC. Owning the ground in Pomona adds a fifth dimension: real estate.

## Why It Matters for NRIs

For the Indian diaspora in Southern California — and there are over 200,000 people of Indian origin in the Greater Los Angeles area alone — the Knight Riders Cricket Ground is the first permanent home for professional cricket within driving distance. Until now, MLC matches in the region relied on temporary venues or converted baseball facilities.

The stadium sits at Fairplex, a 487-acre complex in Pomona best known for the LA County Fair. It is roughly 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles and accessible from both the I-10 and I-210 freeways — a manageable commute for fans in the San Gabriel Valley, Inland Empire, and Orange County, all areas with significant South Asian populations.

The venue is designed for more than cricket. The Knight Riders Group has positioned it as a community hub for entertainment events, family outings, and cultural programming. For a diaspora that has long organized its own cricket matches on municipal pitches and rented turf, having a purpose-built professional venue in the neighbourhood changes the equation.

## The 2028 Olympics Connection

Cricket is returning to the Olympics for the first time since 1900, with the T20 format included at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. The Knight Riders Cricket Ground is expected to play a role in the build-up and potentially in the Games themselves, positioning Pomona as a cricket destination just as the sport makes its biggest push yet into the American mainstream.

The ICC and USA Cricket have been clear that permanent cricket infrastructure in major American metros is a prerequisite for the sport's long-term viability in the country. The Knight Riders have now delivered the first piece of that puzzle.

## What's Next for MLC

Major League Cricket is in its third season, and the league's trajectory is increasingly shaped by franchise investment. San Francisco Unicorns, Texas Super Kings, and now the LA Knight Riders have all made moves to build deeper roots — but no one has gone as far as building from the ground up.

The Knight Riders' next match at their new home ground offers a chance to redeem the batting collapse against Washington Freedom. But the larger story — a Bollywood billionaire building a cricket stadium in the shadow of Hollywood — is the one that will travel. From Kolkata's Eden Gardens to Pomona's Fairplex, the Knight Riders are rewriting what a cricket franchise can be.

For the desi families in the San Gabriel Valley who have spent decades playing tape-ball cricket in parking lots and parks, the Knight Riders just built them a house.
